paragraphs: R’ Yehoshua ben Elisha. (A Tanna of a baraita).

Nazir 44a cites a baraita: the father of R’ Yitzchak (the priest, according to the Rashi gloss cited by Hyman) died in Ginzak. Yitzchak came and asked R’ Yehoshua ben Elisha and the four elders with him. They said: “‘For his father’—when he is whole,” etc. Hyman also cites Moed Katan 20a and the beginning of Semachot, chapter 12, adding the unclear phrase בשעת הסיפור הזה. He says he has already discussed the matter at length under R-A son of R’ Tzadok [ר״א בר׳ צדוק].

notes.text: The supplied בשעת הסיפור הזה clause is unclear; it is not silently replaced from OCR. The cross-reference’s initial ר״א also remains unresolved here. Moed Katan 20a has Rabbi Tzadok asking Elisha ben Avuyah and elders, a different consultation from the Nazir account.

No new primary scalar was returned. The supplied בשעת הסיפור הזה is not silently changed into בשינוי or labelled a proved transcription error; its intended connection remains uncertain. The older recorded Moed Katan comparison names Tzadok asking Elisha ben Avuyah, unlike the Nazir account here; these are not merged. Rashi’s priest gloss is Hyman’s parenthetical attribution, not a newly inspected Rashi witness. Four elders, the father’s death and WHEN HE IS WHOLE remain explicit. Cross-reference ר״א בר׳ צדוק remains R-A son of R’ Tzadok; Elazar and Eliezer are unverified leads, not resolved expansions.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 621) reads בטעות הסיפור הזה, treating the other account as a mistaken form of the story. The supplied Hebrew reads בשעת. The cross-reference is abbreviated there. Hyman discusses these passages under R’ Elazar son of R’ Tzadok (vol. I, pp. 201–202), where he argues that the Nazir version is correct. Rashi on Nazir 44a explicitly calls R’ Yitzchak a priest. Moed Katan names R’ Tzadok and Elisha ben Avuyah, while the consulted Semachot 12 account names R’ Tzadok and records the mourning without identifying anyone he consulted.
